latest_release.body:
Release date: **2026-11-03**

| Release type | Recommended for |
| --- | --- |
| Monthly release | Users of federated query, stream processing, virtual tables, taosX OPC DA, or Kepware ingestion |

## 1. Highlights

- **Federated query**: Linux can query SQL Server and Oracle. Windows can query SQL Server, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and InfluxDB. External tables and virtual-table external sources can use these data sources.
- **Neuron**: taosExplorer can write data collected by Neuron or NeuronEX into TDengine through eKuiper, and complete onboarding, refresh, and monitoring on the Data Collection Agents page.
- **Kepware**: taosExplorer and taosX can connect to Kepware Server 7.1, scan OPC UA points, and ingest them by subscription or polling into a selected database.
- **Security fixes**: Malformed metadata, WAL, query, stream, subscription, and sync input that could crash taosd or cross a buffer is rejected.

## 2. Features

### 2.1 Query, stream processing, and federated query

- Federated query can register on-premises SQL Server 2019 and 2022 as an external source and query its tables and views. On Linux it can also register Oracle. On Windows it can register MySQL, PostgreSQL, InfluxDB, and SQL Server. External tables and virtual-table external sources support these types. See [Federated Query](https://github.com/taosdata/TDengine/blob/ver-3.4.3.9/docs/en/05-tdengine-sql/04-data-query/06-federated-query.md).
- A stream can use a virtual table that references SQL Server columns, and mix those columns with local columns. A short reference and an explicit database or schema reference identify the same remote table. Completed window results are kept after a reference is rebound.
- The new aggregate function `BIT_DURATION` measures how long an integer or boolean point stays in a masked bit state. It can be used in windows and stream processing. Available from `v3.4.3.7`. See [BIT_DURATION](https://github.com/taosdata/TDengine/blob/ver-3.4.3.9/docs/en/05-tdengine-sql/04-data-query/03-function.md#bit_duration).
- `SHOW CREATE TABLE`, `SHOW CREATE STABLE`, `SHOW CREATE VTABLE`, and `SHOW CREATE RSMA` accept `FULL`. With `FULL`, the complete statement is returned as a BLOB and is no longer truncated at 65535 bytes. Without `FULL`, the result is still a truncated VARCHAR. See [SHOW CREATE](https://github.com/taosdata/TDengine/blob/ver-3.4.3.9/docs/en/05-tdengine-sql/09-system-info/03-show.md).
- Every stream notification event includes `triggerTableName`. For `PARTITION BY tbname` it is the trigger child-table name without a database prefix. A virtual child table uses the virtual child-table name. Otherwise the value is an empty string. See [Notification Mechanism in Stream Processing](https://github.com/taosdata/TDengine/blob/ver-3.4.3.9/docs/en/07-stream-processing/01-syntax.md#notification-mechanism-in-stream-processing).

### 2.2 Subscription, ingestion, and taosExplorer

- Table and database subscriptions accept `msg.consume.start.ts`. Only rows whose primary timestamp is at or after that Unix time in milliseconds are consumed. The default is `0`, which does not filter. Column subscriptions are unchanged. See [msg.consume.start.ts](https://github.com/taosdata/TDengine/blob/ver-3.4.3.9/docs/en/10-developer-guide/07-subscription-api.md#msgconsumestartts).
- An OPC DA point task accepts a PI-compatible quality mode and a digital-state value map. Migration tools can rebuild a PI archive on a PI server, then replay and map the points onto existing TDengine tables through OPC DA. See [OPC DA](https://github.com/taosdata/TDengine/blob/ver-3.4.3.9/docs/en/08-data-ingest-and-delivery/01-no-code-ingestion/06-opcda.md).
- taosExplorer can write data collected by Neuron or NeuronEX into TDengine through eKuiper, and complete onboarding, refresh, and monitoring under Data In on the Data Collection Agents page. See [Neuron](https://github.com/taosdata/TDengine/blob/ver-3.4.3.9/docs/en/13-ecosystem-integrations/01-collec
